history.period: 4th century (attested by 608 CE inscription); some accounts credit 9th-century Raja Bhojdev
history.summary: One of the oldest surviving temples in northern India, set between the villages of Goth and Manglod in Jayal tehsil, Nagaur district. An inscription of Gupta year 289 (608 CE), published in Epigraphia Indica, records grants to the goddess by Dahima Brahmins. Tradition holds Dadhimati to be the sister of sage Dadhichi, born of the churning of the sky (dadhi-sagara), who killed the demon Vikatasur; the Kapalapitha Mahatmya identifies her with Lakshmi. She is the kuldevi of the Dadheech/Dahima Brahmins, Kshatriyas and Vaishyas of the region and is counted among the 52 Shaktipeeths in some accounts (verify). The temple interior has early Devi Mahamatya iconography said to predate Kolhapur's Mahalakshmi temple, and depictions of the Valmiki Ramayana. CSV town 'Nagaur' corrected to the actual site Goth-Manglod. Built-date conflict: 4th century per archaeology versus 836-892 CE (Raja Bhojdev) in some sources.

name: Dadhimati Mata Temple
town_description: Goth and Manglod are twin villages in Jayal tehsil of Nagaur district, in the semi-arid Marwar region of Rajasthan; the ancient Dadhimati Mata temple sits between them and is the main pilgrimage focus of the locality.

travel.road: Road from Nagaur city via Jayal; the temple lies between Goth and Manglod villages

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri fairs (Chaitra and Ashwin) draw the largest crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daytime darshan hours typical of rural temples; no published schedule found (verify)
